metadata.title: Charlie Kolar - Out Week 3, but avoiding IR
metadata.description: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said Wednesday that Kolar (forearm) won't play Sunday in Buffalo but is expected to avoid placement on injured reserve, Kris Rhim of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: After undergoing surgery on his fractured left forearm Monday, Kolar had been expected to head to injured reserve and return after missing the minimum four games. However, Harbaugh noted that Kolar ended up receiving a more favorable prognosis than expected once surgery was completed, and the Chargers are now optimistic that the 27-year-old can return to action prior to their Week 7 bye. Kolar will still need to miss at least one game, and with David Njoku (fibula) still ticketed for IR, Oronde Gadsden appears likely to operate as Los Angeles' clear No. 1 tight end for Week 3.

metadata.title: Charlie Kolar (arm) won't go on injured reserve, out for Week 3
metadata.description: Charlie Kolar (arm) won't land on injured reserve but is going to be sidelined for Sunday's game against the Buffalo Bills.
metadata.analysis: The Chargers were initially planning on placing Kolar on injured reserve, but after the procedure on his arm, they feel confident that he won't miss four or more weeks and are opting to keep him on the active roster. He is not going to play in Week 3, but he should be back sometime within the next few weeks, which is less than ideal for the fantasy value of Oronde Gadsden II.

metadata.title: Charlie Kolar (forearm) to undergo surgery, miss at least four weeks
metadata.description: Chargers TE Charlie Kolar is undergoing surgery and plans to return in four weeks.
metadata.analysis: Kolar will aim to return in late October.

metadata.title: Charlie Kolar - Eyeing four-week return from surgery
metadata.description: Kolar plans to undergo surgery to repair a broken forearm and is hopeful to return from injured reserve when first eligible for the Chargers' No. 1 game against the Rams, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: After signing a three-year, $24.3 million deal with the Chargers in March, Kolar had opened the season as the team's top tight end. He mostly operated as a blocker in the Chargers' first two games, contributing three receptions for 21 yards on three targets before exiting the second half of Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Raiders due to the forearm fracture. With Kolar and David Njoku (fibula) both expected to be formally placed on IR within the next few days, Oronde Gadsden is likely to see a major uptick in snaps as the new No. 1 tight end on the depth chart.

metadata.title: Charlie Kolar Undergoing Forearm Surgery
metadata.description: Los Angeles Chargers tight end Charlie Kolar (forearm) is undergoing surgery to fix a broken forearm that he suffered in the Week 2 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders, a source told Jeremy Fowler of ESPN. Kolar plans to make a full return after his four-week stay on short-term Injured Reserve. If Kolar's rehab goes according to plan after surgery, he could be ready to return when he is eligible for the Chargers' game on Nov. 1 against the Los Angeles Rams. In the meantime, with David Njoku (knee) also on IR for the Bolts, Oronde Gadsden now has a clear path to the TE1 role in a Chargers offense that is looking for answers after starting 0-2 in 2026. There was a bit of training camp hype for Kolar in Mike McDaniel's offense this year, but it did not come to fruition through two games, with Kolar sharing snaps with Gadsden and Njoku and catching three passes for 21 yards, with all of that coming on Sunday before he was hurt against the Raiders. Kolar still has a chance to make some noise when he returns from his forearm injury, but it is going to be tough in L.A.'s crowded TE room.

metadata.title: Charlie Kolar (forearm) placed on IR
metadata.description: The Chargers placed TE Charlie Kolar on injured reserve.
metadata.analysis: Kolar suffered the injury in Sunday's game against the Raiders. With David Njoku also on IR, Oronde Gadsden is the only healthy tight end on the Chargers right now.

metadata.title: Charlie Kolar - Will be placed on IR
metadata.description: Head coach Jim Harbaugh said Monday that Kolar will go on injured reserve due to a forearm injury he sustained during Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Raiders, Kris Rhim of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Kolar was spotted with his left arm in a sling following Sunday's loss, and the injury is severe enough for him to warrant a stint on IR. That means he will be forced to miss at least the next four games and is eligible to return for Week 8 against the Rams on Sunday, Nov. 1. David Njoku (knee) is also set to go on IR, leaving Oronde Gadsden as the only healthy tight end on the Chargers' 53-man roster for the time being.

metadata.title: Charlie Kolar Will be Placed on Injured Reserve
metadata.description: Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said on Monday that tight end Charlie Kolar (forearm) will be placed on Injured Reserve after he suffered a forearm injury on Sunday in the Week 2 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders, according to NFL Network's Taylor Bisciotti. The 27-year-old was spotted in the clubhouse wearing a sling on his left arm after Sunday's game, and he will now have to miss at least the next four games. Kolar drew some training camp buzz for his role in new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme before not being targeted in the Week 1 season-opening loss to the Arizona Cardinals. The former fourth-round selection by the Baltimore Ravens in 2022 from Iowa State caught all three of his targets for 21 yards on Sunday against the Raiders before getting injured. With fellow TE David Njoku (leg) also going on IR this week, Oronde Gadsden will now have an excellent opportunity as L.A.'s primary pass-catching tight end, and he should be a popular waiver-wire addition going into the Chargers' Week 3 game against the Buffalo Bills.

metadata.title: Charlie Kolar - Arm in sling after Week 2 loss
metadata.description: Kolar (forearm) was spotted with his left arm in a sling following Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Raiders, Kris Rhim of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Kolar recorded three catches for 21 yards on three targets over 40 snaps on offense before a forearm injury forced him out of the contest in the second half. He was one of two Chargers tight ends to leave the game due to injury, as David Njoku (knee) also made an early departure. Head coach Jim Harbaugh declined to provide updates on Kolar and Njoku after the game, so until the team releases its first Week 3 injury report Wednesday, the statuses of both players will be muddled heading into next Sunday's matchup with the Bills.

metadata.title: Charlie Kolar quiet in loss Sunday
metadata.description: Charlie Kolar caught three passes for 21 yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
metadata.analysis: Kolar wasn't able to get much going on the stat sheet on Sunday, finishing with just 21 yards on three catches against the Raiders. He may see a bit more work than usual moving forward with David Njoku (knee) quite possibly missing time, but he isn't expected to be a strong fantasy option either way.
